offers.name: Dell 15.6" 120Hz Laptop - AMD Ryzen 7 7730U - 16GB DDR4 - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 Home - Carbon Black

praises: 120Hz panel makes Windows feel twice as smooth as every 60Hz rival at this price — scrolling and cursor motion are dramatically better
Ryzen 7 7730U 8C/16T is a genuine multicore performer for the money
SD card reader included — many competitors dropped it
Dell's chassis feels thicker and more rigid than the flimsy HP 15s / Vivobook shells
Single 16GB SO-DIMM leaves a second slot free for a cheap 32GB upgrade
complaints: Wi-Fi 5 (Realtek RTL8821CE 1x1, 802.11ac) in a $1,199 machine in 2026 is indefensible
1.9 kg and 18.9 mm — the heaviest and thickest of the budget 15.6" group
USB-C is data-only; no power delivery or video
120Hz panel is still a TN-class ~250-nit panel: fast but washed out, and the refresh advantage vanishes on battery (Dell caps 60Hz)
No keyboard backlight, soft 720p webcam, and McAfee trial bloat

standouts: Only 120Hz panel in the budget class — smoothest motion on any sub-$1,300 office laptop
dealbreakers: Wi-Fi 5 1x1 in a $1,199 new machine is a genuine hardware embarrassment, not a nitpick
design_philosophy: Dell's budget 15 differentiates on exactly one spec nobody else at this price offers — a 120Hz panel — plus the strongest CPU tier, and pays for it everywhere invisible: an ancient Realtek Wi-Fi 5 1x1 card, a 1.9 kg thick chassis, a data-only USB-C, and no backlight. It is a machine built around a filter-panel checkbox, and the wireless card shows where the margin came from.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-budget-misc.md). Platform-anchored on Ryzen 7 7730U (same calibration as HP 22.json and Aspire Go 10.json): productivity 6.6, gaming 2.1 (Vega 8 benefits slightly from 120Hz smoothness claim excluded). 120Hz nudges screen_quality +0.3 vs TN 60Hz twins; portability penalized for verified 1.9 kg/18.9 mm.
